description:
Programme or Project Overview

Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in neurochemistry with molecular neurobiology. Research in this area studies the molecular organisation of the nervous system - neurotransmitter systems, protein networks at synapses, and the molecular changes underlying neurological and psychiatric disease - using biochemical, cell-biological and imaging approaches on neural cells and tissue models. The position is a salaried four-year employment under the Swedish collective agreement within the university's neuroscience research environment.

Doctoral students in neurochemistry join groups that combine wet-lab molecular work with advanced microscopy and quantitative analysis, often in collaboration with clinically oriented partners studying neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric conditions. Stockholm's neuroscience community spans the university, Karolinska Institutet and Science for Life Laboratory, giving candidates access to national facilities, seminar networks and conference support throughout the doctoral period.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in neuroscience, biochemistry, molecular biology or a related discipline, with laboratory experience in molecular or cell-biological methods. Interest in disease mechanisms and quantitative data analysis is valued. Applications are submitted through the Varbi recruitment system with CV, transcripts, reference contacts and a personal statement describing research experience and motivation.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD employment in neurochemistry
  • Molecular neurobiology of synapses and neurotransmitter systems
  • Disease-mechanism research with clinical collaborators
  • Advanced microscopy and quantitative biochemical methods
  • Stockholm neuroscience network including KI and SciLifeLab
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
